machine: Apple M1 Pro / 32 GB / external exFAT-USB SSD / macOS 26

results.label: MEASURED
results.ttft_note: cold — includes first-run Metal kernel compilation; steady-state prefill is much faster
results.verdict: REPRODUCED thesis: a 3B-active 30B MoE is comfortably interactive on this machine, fully resident, ~17 GB.

results.label: DEFERRED (safety stop, brief §29)
results.status: download reached ~12 GB on SSD (resumable); run NOT executed
results.reason: Internal APFS container had only ~310 MB free (user Data volume = 413 GB of 460 GB) and swap was ~94% used (8.19 of 8.70 GB). Loading a 22 GB-resident model would wire ~22-24 GB, squeeze macOS with swap already exhausted and no disk to grow into -> risk of system hang (not just a killed process). Killed before load.
results.retry_requires: reboot (reclaims the ~8.2 GB swap -> container ~9-10 GB free) OR user frees ~15-20 GB on the internal Data volume; then retry with live memory monitoring + hard abort.

machine_memory_safety_finding.label: MEASURED
machine_memory_safety_finding.note: The real resident-model ceiling on THIS machine is set by internal-disk/swap headroom, NOT the 32 GB RAM. The boot APFS container is chronically ~full (user data = 413 GB), so macOS swap cannot grow and the safe wired set is well under 32 GB. A ~17 GB model (Qwen3-30B-A3B 4-bit) is safe; a ~22 GB model is unsafe until internal space is freed or swap is reclaimed by reboot. This is the binding constraint for the >RAM / resident-80B strategy on this exact setup.
